models_evaluated: five mainstream LLMs (others not named in text)

links.outcome: Consistency of LLM responses across equivalent prompts varying in health literacy signals
links.effect: Responses to low health-literacy signals consistently omitted more key information, gave fewer concrete next steps, and offered less support for independent judgment across five LLMs.
links.quote: Across five mainstream LLMs, models answered all medical questions, but responses to low health-literacy signals consistently omitted more key information, provided fewer concrete next steps, and offered less support for independent judgment.

links.outcome: Information completeness of generative AI responses for users with low health literacy signals
links.effect: Low health-literacy signals led to more omitted key information and fewer concrete next steps, termed Differential Information Dilution (DID).
links.quote: We term this pattern Differential Information Dilution (DID).

unlisted_practices: Knowledge-guided mitigation prompt to reduce information dilution (reduced underinformative simplification most for Claude ~8% and Qwen ~6%)

screen.reason: Evaluates LLM medical question answering across health literacy signals and tests whether a knowledge-guided mitigation prompt reduces differential information dilution.
